היום שאחרי · DIA-378 · slide 1 השער

The stage rail — three changes, and one fork

Every screen below is the real page: the built static export at 390 × 844, with the proposals applied as CSS over it. Nothing here is a redrawn mock, so what you approve is what ships.

20 September 2026 · rendered from out/item/… at commit 4ec3b07 · fixture pool

Where it stands

Bars are 4 × 30px. The step between rungs is 7px — except before the first unreached rung, where it is 25px. That extra 18px is not decoration: the age line is absolutely positioned under its label and hangs 13px below its own row, so without the gap it would collide with the rung beneath. Unreached rungs are a 1.5px dashed outline at 40% white.

The current stage is always the last reached one, so the age line and that gap always land at the same place — the boundary between reached and unreached. That is why they read as one thing.

1 · Unreached rungs, solid grey

The dashed outline is doing badly on a photograph — at 4px wide the dashes break into specks and the rung nearly disappears. Three weights, against the current:

Recommended: rgba(255,255,255,.40). It holds the same weight the dashed border was authored at, so nothing else on the screen shifts in relation to it. .26 disappears against a light sky; the flat #9aa3ad reads nearly as strong as a reached rung, which overstates a stage that has not happened.

2 · One rhythm, age line kept

Removing the 18px step means the age line needs somewhere to go. Raising it 2px — top:26px to 24px — lets a uniform 15px gap clear it with 4px to spare. Three spacings tested:

One thing worth seeing before you pick. A uniform rhythm weakens the age line's attachment to its stage: at 17px it floats midway between יושם and אומת עצמאית and starts to read as belonging to the space rather than to the stage above it. 15px with the line raised keeps it tucked under its own label. 13px clears by 2px — legal, but the age text and the next rung start to crowd.
Recommended: gap 15px, age line at top:24px. Measured across all five fixtures the steps come out [15,15,15,15] with 4px of clearance under the age line — including t06, which is regressed and carries six rungs.

3 · Thicker rungs

Width only — height stays 30px, so the change is the rung's weight, not its size.

Recommended: 6px, with the corner radius going 2px → 3px so the ends stay soft. At 8px the bar is 1:3.75 against its height and starts reading as a block rather than a rung — which works against the spec's reason for having no track behind them, that the stages are not one object.

All three, on every shape the rail takes

Grey at .40, uniform 15px, 6px rungs. The left screen of each pair is what is on dev now.

t01 — four reached, one unreached

t03 — two reached, three unreached

The case with the most grey on screen, and the one where the old dashes were faintest.

t04 — no photograph

The fallback ground is a flat field in the stage colour, so grey has to hold against a colour rather than a photograph.

t06 — regressed, six rungs

The tallest the rail ever gets. At 15px gaps it ends at y=304 against a title block starting at 598, so there is no crowding to worry about.

If you want 8px after all

4 · Head to head — where the age line belongs

Two ways to hold the age line, with grey and thickness settled at .40 and 6px in both.

A — age below the labelB — label and age as one group
What is centred on the rungThe label aloneThe two-line group
Height of that group34.1px29.8px
Group centre vs rung centre9px below0 — exactly on it
Does it fit its own rowNo — hangs 13px pastYes, with 0.1px to spare
Gap the rhythm then needs15px, to clear the overhang10px — nothing to clear
Rail height, five rungs210px190px (today: 196)

The measurement that decides it is the third row. In A the pair sits 9px below the centre of its own rung — the rung lines up with the label and the age hangs off the bottom of it. In B the rung brackets both lines, so the mark and the thing it is marking share an axis.

t01 — current stage last, age at the reached/unreached boundary

t03 — current stage second, age in the middle of the ladder

The harder case: in A the age line sits in a gap with unreached rungs below it, and has to be read back upwards to find the stage it belongs to.

Why not B at 7px, which the numbers allow. Because the group no longer overhangs, B could keep the original 7px rhythm and make the rail shorter still. At 6px wide and 7px apart the grey rungs start to close into a dotted line — and §4's reason for having no track behind the rungs is that “a continuous line reads as one object and the stages are not one object.” 10px keeps them discrete.
Recommended: B at 10px. It is the only option where the age line is attached to its stage by geometry rather than by proximity, it holds on all five fixture shapes including the six-rung regressed one, and it ends up 6px shorter than the rail on dev today rather than 14px taller.

Full screens

What changes in the code

All of it is app/globals.css, plus one dead class in Gate.tsx. Written for B at 10px; for A, the row-gap is 15px and only the top on span b changes instead of the two rules beneath it.

.deck-gate-rail {
-  grid-template-columns: 4px 1fr; column-gap: 9px; row-gap: 7px;
+  grid-template-columns: 6px 1fr; column-gap: 9px; row-gap: 10px;
}

.deck-gate-rung > i {
-  border-radius: 2px;
+  border-radius: 3px;
}

.deck-gate-rung > i.off {
-  background: none; border: 1.5px dashed rgba(255,255,255,.4);
+  background: rgba(255,255,255,.40);
}

-.deck-gate-rung.deck-gate-gap > i,
-.deck-gate-rung.deck-gate-gap > span { margin-top: 18px }

.deck-gate-rung > span {
-  height: 30px; display: flex; align-items: center;
+  height: 30px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center;
+  text-align: right; line-height: 1.2;
}

.deck-gate-rung > span b {
-  position: absolute; top: 26px; right: 0;
+  position: static; display: block; margin-top: 1px;
}
One deliberate choice in there. The label stays right-aligned with text-align: right rather than a flex cross-axis property. §2's RTL trap is exactly this: align-items: flex-end would resolve left on this page and silently put every stage name on the wrong side. The physical property cannot be got wrong.

With the gap gone, deck-gate-gap has nothing left to do — the class and the firstUnreached lookup that applies it come out of Gate.tsx too. Deleting them is part of the change, not a tidy-up for later: a class that survives its rule is the next person's confusion.

What this changes in the spec

Two sentences are now wrong, in two files, and both describe the rail rather than the gate — so slides 3 and 4 inherit them when their locator is built in Phases 5 and 6. They should be fixed in the same change, not after.

WhereWhat it saysWhat it should say
mobile-item.html §4 “an unreached rung is dashed and preceded by a deliberate gap” Unreached rungs are solid grey; the rail keeps one rhythm throughout
mobile-item.html §6 “An unreached stage gets the same tag as a dashed outline in muted ink” This is the stage tag on slides 3 and 4, not the rung — check whether you want it to follow the rail, or stay dashed where it is a page title rather than a mark
The §6 one is a real question, not a copy-edit. The dashed treatment appears twice in the design: on the rung, and on the status tag that titles an unreached stage page. They were dashed for the same reason. If the rung stops being dashed and the tag does not, the page stops saying one thing — but a dashed tag is also doing a different job, on a surface with no photograph under it. Worth a look when slide 4 gets built; it does not block this change.
